title.en: There is / there are and it is
title.es: There is / there are e it is

summary.en: Use **there is / there are** to say that something exists or to introduce it for the first time: _There is a pharmacy on the corner._ Use **it** to talk about something already known, and also for weather, time, distance and "it is + adjective + to…": _It's raining_, _It's difficult to park here._ Spanish _hay_ is always **there is/are**, never _is_ or _it is_ on its own.
summary.es: «Hay» = there is / there are. «Es» o «está» referido a algo ya conocido = it is. No puedes empezar con is: siempre hace falta there o it.

form: **There is** + singular or uncountable; **there are** + plural: _There is a problem. There are two options._
Questions: **Is there…? / Are there…?**; negatives: **There isn't a… / There aren't any…**
Past and perfect: **there was / were**, **there has been / have been**
**It is** + adjective + **to** + verb: _It is important to book early._
**It** for weather, time, distance, dates: _It's 8.30. It's ten miles to the airport._

uses.text: **Introduce something new** → there is/are: _There's a message for you on the desk._
**Talk about it once it is known** → it: _I found a flat. **It**'s near the station._

note.en: First there is (new information), then it (the same thing again).
note.es: Primero there is (algo nuevo); después, it (ya lo conoces).

uses.text: **Weather, time and distance** → it: _It's getting dark._ _It's a long way to the coast._
**General comments** → it + adjective + to…: _It's hard to find good staff._ _It was nice to see you._
**Quantity** → there + a lot of / any / no: _There wasn't any time._ _There are a lot of tourists in August._

mistakes.wrong: In my city has a big park.
mistakes.right: There is a big park in my city.

why.en: Has cannot mean "there is". Use there is / there are.
why.es: «Hay» no es has: se dice there is / there are.

mistakes.wrong: Is a lot of traffic at this time.
mistakes.right: There is a lot of traffic at this time.

why.en: English needs a subject, so use there.
why.es: No se puede empezar con is: hace falta there.

mistakes.wrong: It is a lot of people in the square.
mistakes.right: There are a lot of people in the square.

why.en: Existence is expressed with there, not it. People is plural, so use are.
why.es: Para «hay», usa there. Y people es plural: there are.

mistakes.wrong: Is difficult to find a flat in this area.
mistakes.right: It is difficult to find a flat in this area.

why.en: Use it as the subject before an adjective.
why.es: «Es difícil encontrar…» = It is difficult to find…

mistakes.wrong: There have two bedrooms and a small kitchen.
mistakes.right: There are two bedrooms and a small kitchen. / It has two bedrooms and a small kitchen.

why.en: There have is never correct. Say there is/are, or use it has for a known place.
why.es: There have no existe. O there are, o it has si hablas de un sitio concreto.

examples.en: There's a good Italian restaurant behind the station.
examples.es: Hay un buen restaurante italiano detrás de la estación.

examples.en: Is there a bank near here? Yes, it's opposite the library.
examples.es: ¿Hay un banco por aquí? Sí, está enfrente de la biblioteca.

examples.en: There aren't any tickets left for Saturday.
There was nobody at reception when we arrived.
There have been several complaints about the noise.
It's about forty minutes from here to the airport.
It was raining all weekend, so we stayed in.
It's essential to arrive early on the day of the exam.
How many people are there in your team?
It looks as if there will be a delay.

practice.prompt: ___ a lot of traffic on the ring road this morning.

explanation.en: Existence is expressed with there was; every sentence needs a subject.

practice.prompt: I'd love to visit Granada. ___ is a beautiful city.

explanation.en: Granada is already known, so we refer to it with it.

practice.prompt: ___ difficult to park in the centre at weekends.

explanation.en: It is + adjective + to + verb is the pattern for general comments.

practice.prompt: Excuse me, ___ a chemist near here?

explanation.en: A question about existence uses Is there…? with the verb first.
